ahead: MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT_REVIEW.md found a defect in MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT.md section 3, equation (4)/(5): the model-side error O(r E_md(1+R/r)) inside H_chi gets multiplied by the outer sqrt(r) from the Gauss-sum step just like the F_chi side's N*Upsilon(r) term does, giving O(R^{3/2} E_md), not the printed O(R E_md). This propagates to section 4's squared bound (R^3 e^{-2 sqrt(l)/3} in place of R^2 e^{-2 sqrt(l)/3}) and tightens the compatibility condition in section 4 and in (H) from c_0 <= 2/9 to c_0 <= 1/6. It does not appear to break the boxed result (S'') itself, since c_0 is described as TT's own small threshold constant, well under 1/6 in any case, but the paper's own numeric check of its hypothesis is wrong as printed and should be corrected before anyone else builds on the exact value 2/9. Also flagged (not a defect, an imprecision): section 5's closing sentence calls the corollary 'the non-existence of Siegel zeros in the classical form' without repeating the even-character/odd-conductor restriction stated two sentences earlier in the same paragraph; the restriction is real (the proof uses tau(tilde chi)=sqrt(q~) for even tilde chi and mu(q~)=+-1 for odd squarefree q~) and should be carried into that sentence.

work.what: In hunts/prime_pair_error/MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT.md, fix the sqrt(r) bookkeeping error identified in hunts/prime_pair_error/MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT_REVIEW.md item (2). Equation (4)'s passage from H_chi(theta) = delta_chi K_N(theta) - ... + O(r E_md(1+R/r)) to the bound |W(alpha)| <= sqrt(r) max_chi |F_chi - H_chi| + O(l^2) needs the sqrt(r) factor applied to the H_chi error term too, since it enters the same character sum with the same Gauss-sum coefficient tau(chi-bar) of size sqrt(r) that the F_chi-side error N*Upsilon(r) already correctly carries in the boxed equation (5) as sqrt(r)*N*Upsilon(r). The corrected size is sqrt(r) * O(r E_md (1+R/r)) which at r=R is O(R^{3/2} E_md), not the printed O(R E_md) (a ratio of sqrt(r), unbounded as R grows, so this is not a matter of a loose but valid inequality). Concretely: replace '8R E_md' by '8 R^{3/2} E_md' in equation (4) and in the boxed equation (5); replace the term 'R^2 N^2 e^{-2 sqrt(l)/3}' by 'R^3 N^2 e^{-2 sqrt(l)/3}' in the squared bound sup_M|W|^2 in section 4; recompute the sixth exponent accordingly (it becomes 2/3 - 3*sigma instead of 2/3 - 2*sigma, since R^3 e^{-2 sqrt(l)/3} = e^{-(2/3-3 sigma) sqrt l} with R=e^{sigma sqrt l}); and replace the compatibility condition 'c_0 <= 2/9' by 'c_0 <= 1/6' both in section 4's prose and in the boxed hypothesis (H) at the top of the document (currently 'c_0 <= min(2/9, sqrt(c)/2, sqrt(b)/2, c_P)', the 2/9 should become 1/6). Check whether the boxed result (S'') and its stated exponent still go through with this corrected, tighter, compatibility hypothesis; it should, since TT's actual c_0 is a very small absolute constant well under 1/6, but this should be verified and stated rather than assumed. Also correct section 5's closing sentence, which currently reads 'That is an effective zero-free interval (1-c'/log q~,1) for real zeros of real characters, i.e. the non-existence of Siegel zeros in the classical form,' by adding the even-character, odd-conductor qualification that the same paragraph already states in the Proposition's hypothesis (tilde_chi(-1)=1, tilde_q odd), e.g. 'for even primitive real characters of odd conductor' in place of 'for real characters,' since the proof genuinely does not cover odd characters (an explicit remark right after equation (7) says the odd case needs either an extra loss of a log factor or a different, |W|^4-based, route, neither carried out) or characters of even conductor (the argument uses q~ odd squarefree throughout, for the exact identity mu(q~)=+-1 and to avoid the separate mod 4 / mod 8 cases that SIEGEL_UNIFORMITY.md section 4 treats differently). Do not touch anything else in the document; both defects are narrow, quotable fixes, not the shape of the whole argument. Read hunts/prime_pair_error/MAJOR_ARC_EXPLICIT_REVIEW.md items (2), (4) and (5) in full for the exact derivations before editing.
